title: A New Approach for Surface Urban Heat Island Monitoring Based on Machine Learning Algorithm and Spatiotemporal Fusion Model
Surface urban heat island intensity in five major cities of Bangladesh: Patterns, drivers and trends
authors: Ashraf Dewan; Grigory Kiselev; Dirk Botje; Golam Iftekhar Mahmud; Md. Hanif Bhuian; Quazi K. Hassan
study_objective: Examine annual and monthly day/night SUHII between 2000 and 2019, determine controlling factors, and assess temporal trends across five major Bangladesh cities.
bangladesh_relevance: Direct Bangladesh multi-city SUHII benchmark using 20 years of MODIS.
study_area_boundary_source: Planning boundaries from relevant city development authorities
climate_or_seasonal_context: Annual and monthly day/night SUHII; dry months contrasted with wet months
data_sources: MOD11A2 v006; MCD12Q1; MOD09A1; MCD19A2; MCD43A3; MOD44B; LandScan; DMSP-OLS; VIIRS
satellite_sensors: MODIS products plus DMSP-OLS and VIIRS nighttime lights
ancillary_data: LandScan population; planning boundaries; nighttime lights
cloud_filtering: Clear-sky pixels only; retained MODIS LST error <= 2 K
resampling: All datasets harmonized to 1 km nominal resolution
lst_method: MOD11A2 product-based LST; SUHII as urban-rural difference
emissivity_method: Generalized split-window retrieval from MODIS bands 31 and 32
thermal_constants: MODIS v006 quality filter with LST error <= 2 K
ndwi_method: MOD09A1-derived NDWI aggregated monthly and annually
other_indices: EVI; BCI; MSI; VCF; AOD; population; nighttime lights
lulc_classes: IGBP classes reclassified to urban and non-urban
lulc_algorithm: MODIS IGBP reclassification into urban and non-urban
accuracy_assessment: Product-derived; no separate classification accuracy table
meteorological_integration: No station meteorology; AOD used as environmental driver
correlation_analysis: Pearson correlation between SUHII and candidate drivers
trend_analysis: Mann-Kendall annual and monthly trend tests
performance_metrics: Across-city day-night relationship R2 = 0.50, p = 0.00; Pearson r values by city
lst_range_c: Raw LST range not reported; SUHII magnitudes reported instead
correlation_results: Across-city day versus night R2 = 0.50 (p = 0.00); Dhaka daytime population differential r = 0.92
temperature_difference_c: Annual daytime SUHII Dhaka 2.74 C and Chittagong 1.92 C; nighttime Chittagong 1.90 C and Dhaka 1.57 C
bangladesh_specific_parameters: Dry months generally show stronger SUHII than wet months
limitations: No in-situ UHI measurements; remotely sensed drivers only; monsoon cloudiness reduces valid pixel counts
key_findings: Dhaka and Chittagong show the highest annual SUHII; daytime SUHII exceeds nighttime; population, imperviousness, and lack of greenness are major drivers.
thesis_use_notes: BP2; direct Bangladesh comparative benchmark for SUHII design and driver interpretation

title: Prospective Mitigation Interventions of Urban Heat Island in a Megacity: A Machine Learning Approach To Inform Climate Resilience in Dhaka, Bangladesh
authors: A. S. M. Maksud Kamal; Shamsuddin Shahid; Anika Tabassum; Jakir Hossain
study_location: Dhaka Metropolitan Area / Greater Dhaka City
study_objective: Analyze spatiotemporal UHI dynamics in Dhaka from 1990 to 2023 and evaluate mitigation strategies using Landsat-derived indices and machine learning.
bangladesh_relevance: Direct Dhaka-focused multi-year LST, index, and machine-learning mitigation study.
study_area_boundary_source: District, upazila, and study area shapefiles; DIVA-GIS mentioned
data_sources: Google Earth Engine Landsat archive; Google Earth Pro; study area shapefiles; climate records
satellite_sensors: Landsat 5 TM; Landsat 7 ETM+; Landsat 8 OLI/TIRS
ancillary_data: Google Earth Pro imagery; study area shapefiles; climate records
cloud_filtering: Not fully detailed in first extraction pass
atmospheric_correction: Handled through GEE and Landsat processing chain; exact version not extracted in first pass
cross_sensor_normalization: Multi-sensor TM, ETM+, and OLI/TIRS workflow
emissivity_method: Surface emissivity term within SMW linearized radiative transfer equation
lulc_source_imagery: Landsat series interpreted through indices and maps
lulc_classes: Urbanized, vegetated, water, and related thermal classes interpreted from maps
lulc_algorithm: No standalone supervised classifier reported; index-based thermal interpretation
training_sample_source: Field observations used to verify land cover classes and hot/cool spots
accuracy_assessment: Model metrics plus field verification; no confusion matrix extracted
meteorological_integration: Climate records mentioned but first-pass extraction did not recover station details
correlation_analysis: Correlation matrix for LST versus NDVI, NDWI, NDBI, UI, and Albedo
trend_analysis: Multi-year spatiotemporal comparison of LST and indices
machine_learning_workflow: Linear Regression; SVM; Random Forest; ANN
lst_range_c: Approximately 19 C to 35 C for the 2023 reference Landsat 8 map
correlation_results: LST inversely related to NDVI, NDWI, and Albedo; directly related to UI and NDBI
temperature_difference_c: 10 percent NDBI reduction may reduce LST by up to 2 C; 10 percent UI reduction about 0.5 C; 25 percent NDVI increase may reduce ambient temperature by 2-3 C
bangladesh_specific_parameters: 20 percent increase in NDVI and NDWI can reduce LST by about 12 percent and 7 percent, respectively
limitations: Data and model uncertainties acknowledged; no full in-situ LST validation extracted in first pass
sensitivity_analysis: Sobol variance-based sensitivity analysis with +/- 25 percent test range
key_findings: SVM is the strongest LST predictor in Dhaka; NDVI, NDWI, and Albedo cool while UI and NDBI warm; mitigation scenarios suggest meaningful temperature reduction from greening and reduced imperviousness.
thesis_use_notes: P1; direct Dhaka multi-year Landsat plus ML mitigation benchmark

title: Understanding Urban Heat Islands in Dhaka City Through Explainable GeoAI
authors: Maria Sultana; Md Didarul Islam; Bradford Johnson
study_objective: Model and interpret spatially heterogeneous LST variation across Dhaka using explainable GeoAI.
bangladesh_relevance: Direct Dhaka explainable-ML benchmark for feature importance and spatial heterogeneity.
study_area_boundary_source: Dhaka city divided into 500 m by 500 m grid cells
climate_or_seasonal_context: Summer median composite for 2020 in a tropical monsoon city
data_sources: Landsat 8 TIRS/OLI; Google Open Buildings; Meta Canopy Height; Dynamic World
satellite_sensors: Landsat 8 TIRS/OLI plus ancillary geospatial datasets
ancillary_data: Building area ratio; bare land percentage; water percentage; tree cover above 2 m; spatial coordinates
resampling: Variables aggregated to 500 m grid; canopy resampled to 10 m first
seasonal_harmonization: Summer median composite to reduce cloud noise
lst_method: Landsat 8 mono-window algorithm with NDVI-based emissivity correction
emissivity_equation: NDVI-based emissivity correction within mono-window LST equation
wavelength_parameter: rho = 1.438 x 10^-2 m K reported; wavelength term included
ndwi_method: Water percentage derived from Dynamic World classes, not direct NDWI
other_indices: Building_area_ratio; bare_pct; water_pct; tree_cover_gt2m_pct; SHAP; GeoShapley
lulc_classes: Water and bare land classes explicitly aggregated to grid percentages
lulc_algorithm: Dynamic World class aggregation to 500 m grid; no new supervised classifier
post_classification_refinement: Reclassification and aggregation to 500 m cells
accuracy_assessment: Predictive model metrics rather than standalone classification accuracy
correlation_analysis: Correlation matrix between mean LST and environmental / urban variables
machine_learning_workflow: FLAML AutoML with LightGBM; 80:20 split; 5-fold cross-validation
feature_selection: Predictors were bare_pct, water_pct, tree_cover_gt2m_pct, mean_NDVI, building_area_ratio, and X/Y spatial coordinates
lst_range_c: Not reported numerically in first pass
correlation_results: Built area ratio strongest warming predictor; NDVI, water, and tree cover show cooling behavior with spatial heterogeneity
thresholds: Bare land impact rises beyond about 10 percent; water cooling strengthens beyond about 20 percent; NDVI cooling strongest from about 0.2 to 0.5; tree cover above 30 percent shows clearer cooling
bangladesh_specific_parameters: 500 m Dhaka grid; summer Landsat 8 median composite
limitations: Residual spatial effects imply missing factors such as wind corridors, albedo, and building configuration
key_findings: LightGBM explains about 72.5 percent of Dhaka mean LST variance and GeoShapley reveals strong spatial heterogeneity in built-up, bare land, water, and vegetation effects.
thesis_use_notes: P3; direct Dhaka explainable GeoAI benchmark for advanced modeling and interpretability
